source.title: CM values of higher automorphic Green functions for orthogonal groups
source.authors: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Stephan Ehlen and Tonghai Yang
readSections: Published version (open access, CC BY 4.0), read in full on 2026-09-22 (PDF SHA-256 729e4f9daff82e8e98ae27bcd8084c4e89c8a08b91f2b5106c048ab35cda4160). Statement numbers and pages are the published ones; the appendix is Section 9 there.

arXiv v2 TeX source (SHA-256 8a0bf7ad73146f2c37e9b0c509ee66d6af7cf63537d7d66c6b32123ba064be04) was used as a reading aid. A word-level diff shows that it matches the published text up to layout and one sentence added after Lemma 7.2 (the formula for χ_Δ when gcd(a, b, c, Δ) = 1).

Checked in detail: Lemma 3.1, Proposition 3.6, the proofs of Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.4, Corollary 5.9, Proposition 6.2, the Gamma factors of Lemma 6.3 and Theorem 6.5, Proposition 6.7 and Lemma 6.8 (symbolically, j ≤ 5), Proposition 6.16, the constants in Theorem 7.9, (7.10), Theorem 7.11 and Example 3, the counting in Corollary 7.18, and Proposition 9.6. The cited results of Bruinier (LNM 1780), Oda–Tsuzuki, Kudla–Yang, Bruinier–Yang, Zhang, Xue, Howard, Duke–Jenkins, Alfes-Neumann–Schwagenscheidt and Howard–Madapusi Pera were used as quoted.

summary: Bruinier, Ehlen and Yang study the Gross–Zagier conjecture that CM values of the higher Green functions G_{j+1,f} on X(1)² are logarithms of algebraic numbers in class fields. Their tool is the higher regularized theta lift Φ^j(z, h, f) = (4π)^{−j}Φ(z, h, R^jf) on orthogonal Shimura varieties of signature (n, 2), which realizes higher Green functions (Proposition 4.7). At a small CM point it is CT⟨f, [θ_P, 𝒢^+_N(τ, h)]_j⟩ for any preimage 𝒢_N of the binary theta function under the lowering operator (Theorem 5.5). On the whole CM cycle it is CT⟨f^+, [θ_P, 𝓔^+_N]_j⟩ − L′(ξf, U, 0) with the incoherent Eisenstein series (Theorem 5.4); a big-CM analogue exists for real quadratic F (Theorem 5.10). The appendix builds preimages 𝒢_N whose coefficients are logarithms of algebraic numbers in the ring class field with Shimura reciprocity (Theorem 3.9/9.4), via a see-saw to signature (1, 2) and Borcherds products. Consequences: the conjecture for CM points in one imaginary quadratic field (Theorem 6.1, strengthening Viazovska); partial averages over CM points of a fundamental discriminant d_1, twisted by genus characters, via Zagier lifts and Millson theta lifts (Theorems 1.2, 7.11, 7.13, Corollary 7.15); the full conjecture when the class group of d_1 has exponent ≤ 2 (Corollary 1.4/7.18); and a higher-weight Gross–Kohnen–Zagier theorem for Zhang's higher Heegner cycles on Kuga–Sato varieties (Theorems 1.9, 6.5, 6.12), from the archimedean formula plus Xue's and Howard's finite intersections. The atlas plans Weil representations and theta kernels (MP.4–MP.5), harmonic Maass forms and Jacobi forms (QM.3, QM.1), CM points (HE.1), canonical models (V4, V6) and Kuga–Sato varieties (GH.0). It has no higher Green functions or their CM values. Routes: the paper coalesces into HigherGreenFunctionCMValues, the Part II of Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights proposed by PAPER-LI-23 (which builds on this paper). Genus characters and genus theory go to GN.2, binary Siegel–Weil to MP.6, the Shimura correspondence to MP.7, the incoherent weight-1 Eisenstein series to GZ.6, and Heegner divisors over Z with their intersections to GZ.7. Six source issues are recorded, all in the published text. The constant for odd j in Theorems 7.11 and 7.13 is inconsistent with (7.10) and with Example 3: it should be 2^{j−2}, not −2^{j−1}. Corollaries 1.4 and 7.18 (and Theorem 6.1) omit the hypothesis (z, z′) ∉ Z^j(f). Lemma 6.3 drops a factor √M. Lemma 6.8's recursion is misprinted. Corollary 7.18's proof counts s genus characters instead of 2^{s−1}. (7.6) omits the weight χ_Δ.

items.name: Elliptic modular forms, the Gamma function and the Gauss hypergeometric function
items.statement: Holomorphic modular and cusp forms for SL_2(Z) (E_4, E_8, E_10, Δ), the upper half-plane and its fundamental domain, the Gamma function and the Gauss hypergeometric function F(a, b, c; z).
items.note: Mathlib: UpperHalfPlane, ModularForm, CuspForm, ModularForm.eisensteinSeriesMF, Complex.Gamma, ordinaryHypergeometric. Weakly holomorphic and vector-valued forms, the j-function, Legendre functions Q_{s−1} and the Whittaker functions M_{κ,μ} are not in Mathlib.

items.name: The Weil representation ρ_L of Mp_2(Z) and vector-valued modular forms
items.statement: For an even lattice L, ρ_L on S_L = C[L′/L] with ρ_L(T)φ_μ = e(Q(μ))φ_μ and ρ_L(S)φ_μ = e((2−n)/8)|L′/L|^{−1/2}Σ_ν e(−(μ,ν))φ_ν, identified with the conjugate of the finite Weil representation on S(V(A_f)); the Petersson slash operator |_{k,ρ_L}.
items.note: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.4 plans the adelic cover and global Weil representation.

items.name: Siegel theta functions θ_L(τ, z, h)
items.statement: θ(τ, z, h, φ) = v Σ_{x∈V(Q)} e(Q(x_{z⊥})τ + Q(x_z)τ̄)φ(h^{−1}x) and θ_L = Σ_μ θ(·, φ_μ)φ_μ, a non-holomorphic modular form of weight n/2 − 1 with representation ρ_L, descending to X_K when K stabilizes L̂ and acts trivially on L′/L.
items.note: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.5 plans theta kernels and convergence.

items.name: Harmonic Maass forms, ξ_k, Hejhal–Poincaré series and the exact sequence
items.statement: Weak Maass forms of weight k for (Mp_2(Z), ρ_L) (Laplace eigenfunctions of at most exponential growth); harmonic ones; ξ_k(f) = v^{k−2} conj(L_k f); f = f^+ + f^−; H_{k,ρ_L} ⊃ M^! ⊃ M ⊃ S with 0 → M^!_{k,ρ_L} → H_{k,ρ_L} → S_{2−k,ρ̄_L} → 0; the Hejhal–Poincaré series F_{m,μ}(τ, s, k) built from 𝓜_{s,k}(v) = v^{−k/2}M_{−k/2,s−1/2}(v), a harmonic Maass form at s_0 = 1 − k/2 with principal part e(−mτ)(φ_μ + φ_{−μ}).
items.note: QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3 plans harmonic Maass forms, ξ and Poincaré series.

items.name: Weak Jacobi forms φ̃_{−2,1}, φ̃_{0,1} and the theta decomposition
items.statement: J^!_{k,1} ≅ M^!_{k−1/2, ρ̄_P} for P = Z with Q(x) = x² (Eichler–Zagier), and the ring of weak Jacobi forms of even weight is generated over M_* by φ̃_{−2,1} and φ̃_{0,1} (Eichler–Zagier Thm. 9.3), with φ̃_{−2,1}(τ, 0) = 0 and φ̃_{0,1}(τ, 0) = 12.
items.note: QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.1 plans theta, eta and Jacobi forms.

items.name: CM points, ring class fields and complex multiplication
items.statement: For a discriminant d < 0, CM points of discriminant d on X_0(1) are defined over the ring class field H_d of O_d, and Cl(O_D) ≅ k_D^×\A^×_{k_D,f}/Ô_D^× ≅ Gal(H_D/k_D) acts on them by the main theorem of complex multiplication (Cox §15.E).
items.note: HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.1 plans CM points and descent to ring class fields.

items.name: Canonical models of GSpin Shimura varieties and Shimura reciprocity
items.statement: X_K = H(Q)\(D × H(A_f)/K) for H = GSpin(V), V of signature (n, 2), is the complex points of a Shimura variety of dimension n with a canonical model over Q, the CM cycles Z(U) are defined over Q, and the Galois action on CM values of Borcherds products is given by Shimura reciprocity (Shimura, Thm. 6.31).
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V4 plans canonical models with the special-point reciprocity condition, and V6 plans Hodge and abelian type.

items.name: Kuga–Sato varieties over modular curves
items.statement: For M a product of two coprime integers > 2, the universal elliptic curve over 𝒳(M) extends to a regular semistable 𝓔(M); the Kuga–Sato variety 𝒴 = 𝒴_κ(M) is a canonical resolution of the (2κ − 2)-fold fibre product of 𝓔(M) over 𝒳(M) (Zhang §2).
items.note: GeneralizedHeegnerCycles GH.0 plans the desingularized fibre powers of the universal elliptic curve.

items.name: Proposition 3.8 and (3.10)–(3.12): Siegel–Weil and incoherent Eisenstein series for binary lattices
items.statement: For V of signature (0, 2) and L ⊂ V even, E_L(τ, s; ℓ) = Σ_{Γ′_∞\Γ′}[v^{(s+1−ℓ)/2}φ_0]|_{ℓ,ρ_L}γ satisfies R_ℓE(s; ℓ) = ½(s+1+ℓ)E(s; ℓ+2) and L_ℓE(s; ℓ) = ½(s+1−ℓ)E(s; ℓ−2). With Tamagawa measure (vol SO(V)(Q)\SO(V)(A_f) = 2), ∫θ_L(τ, h)dh = E_L(τ, 0; −1) (Proposition 3.8, Kudla).
items.note: MP.6 plans reusable theta integrals and the local–global comparison; PAPER-LI-23 routes the (n, 2) Siegel–Weil formula there too.

items.name: The derivative E′_L(τ, 0; 1) of the incoherent Eisenstein series and its Fourier coefficients
items.statement: L_1E_L(τ, s; 1) = (s/2)E_L(τ, s; −1), so 𝓔_L = E′_L(τ, 0; 1) is a harmonic Maass form of weight 1 with L_1𝓔_L = ½E_L(τ, 0; −1); its holomorphic part 𝓔^+_L = Σκ(m, μ)q^mφ_μ has coefficients κ(m, μ), (m, μ) ≠ (0, 0), that are (up to a common rational factor) logarithms of positive rational numbers (Kudla–Yang; Bruinier–Yang Thm. 2.6). For real quadratic F, E′_N(τ⃗, 0; 1) with L_{1,i}E′_N(τ⃗, 0; 1) = ½E_N(τ⃗, 0; 1(i)) and its holomorphic part (Bruinier–Kudla–Yang Prop. 4.6).
items.note: GZ.6 plans 'incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms'. These are the weight-1 incoherent kernels.

items.name: Definition 7.1 and Lemmas 7.2–7.3: local genus characters χ_Δ
items.statement: For a fundamental discriminant Δ and λ = [[b/2, −a], [c, −b/2]] ∈ L′_p with 4Q(λ) ∈ ΔZ_p, χ_{Δ,p}(λ) = (n, Δ)_p if gcd(a, b, c, Δ) = 1 and [a, b, c] represents n with (Δ, n) = 1, and 0 otherwise; χ_Δ = ∏_p χ_{Δ,p}. Lemma 7.2: χ_{Δ,p} is well defined and for p | Δ equals (a, Δ)_p if p ∤ a, (c, Δ)_p if p ∤ c, and 0 otherwise; on L it is the classical genus character (Gross–Kohnen–Zagier I.2). Lemma 7.3: χ_{Δ,p}(h·λ) = (det h, Δ)_p χ_{Δ,p}(λ) for h ∈ GL_2(Z_p).
items.locator: Lemma 7.2, p. 752; Definition 7.1, p. 752; Lemma 7.3, p. 753
items.note: Classical genus theory of binary quadratic forms (the Lemma 7.2 proof is 'left to the reader'). GN.2 owns genera and local invariants of quadratic forms.

items.name: Genus theory: class groups of exponent 2
items.statement: For a negative fundamental discriminant D′ with s prime divisors, the genus characters χ_Δ (D′ = Δ·Δ̃ with Δ, Δ̃ fundamental) are the characters of Cl(O_{D′})/Cl(O_{D′})²; if Cl(O_{D′}) has exponent ≤ 2 then h(D′) = 2^{s−1}, every class-group character is a genus character, and H_{D′} = k_{D′}(√Δ_1, …, √Δ_{2^{s−1}}).
items.note: Gauss's genus theory. GN.2 owns genera of binary quadratic forms.

items.name: The Shimura lift Shim_{m_0,μ_0} for vector-valued half-integral weight forms
items.statement: For L of signature (1, 2) and level 4M, Shim_{m_0,μ_0}: S_{3/2+2j,ρ_L} → S_{2+4j}(Γ_0(M)), g ↦ Σ_n Σ_{d|n} d^{2j}(D_0/d)b(m_0n²/d², μ_0n/d)q^n (Gross–Kohnen–Zagier II.3), with L(Shim(g), s) = L(χ_{D_0}, s − 2j)Σ_n b(m_0n², μ_0n)n^{−s}; Hecke-equivariance and a linear combination of these maps giving an isomorphism of newform spaces S^{new}_{3/2+2j,ρ_L} ≅ S^{−,new}_{2+4j}(Γ_0(M)) (Skoruppa–Zagier), with L(Shim(g), s) = b(m_0, μ_0)L(G, s) for corresponding newforms.
items.note: MP.7 plans half-integral weight forms, their metaplectic Fourier coefficients and twists; the Shimura correspondence belongs there.

items.name: Heegner divisors over Z: the moduli stacks 𝒵(m, μ), 𝒞 and 𝒵(m, 𝔞, μ)
items.statement: 𝒵(m, μ) classifies cyclic M-isogenies π: E → E′ with an O_D-action ι satisfying ι(𝔫)ker π = 0, 𝔫 = [M, (r+√D)/2]; 𝒵(m, μ)_C = P_{D,r} + P_{D,−r}. 𝒞 classifies (E, ι: O_{D_0} ↪ End E) with the main involution inducing complex conjugation; 𝒞 ≅ 𝒵(m_0, μ_0) (Bruinier–Yang Lemma 7.10), a closed substack of 𝒳_0(M). 𝒵(m, 𝔞, μ) ⊂ 𝒞 adds a special endomorphism β ∈ L(E, ι)(1/√D_0)𝔞 with Nm β = m Nm 𝔞 and μ + β ∈ O_E𝔞 (Bruinier–Yang §6; Kudla–Yang §2.4).
items.note: GZ.7 plans CM intersection multiplicities with deformation lengths via Serre–Tate.

items.name: Lemma 6.10: Heegner divisors are Cartier and equal to the Zariski closure
items.statement: Let c be the conductor of O_D and M′ = (M, c). Then 𝒵(m, μ) ≅ Z̄(m, μ), the Zariski closure of Z(m, μ) in 𝒳_0(M), as stacks over Z[1/M′].
items.locator: Lemma 6.10, p. 745; proof pp. 745–746 (due to B. Howard)
items.note: Uses Serre–Tate, Howard's deformation theorem (Math. Ann. 2012, Thm. 2.1.3) for p ∤ c, Serre–Tate coordinates for split p | c, and Wewers's Prop. 5.1 for supersingular p | c.

items.name: Lemma 6.11 and Proposition 6.9: finite intersections of higher Heegner cycles
items.locator: Proposition 6.9, p. 744; Lemma 6.11, p. 747; proof of Proposition 6.9, pp. 747–748
items.note: The arithmetic degree of 𝒵(m, 𝔞, μ) is a Fourier coefficient of 𝓔^+ (Bruinier–Yang Thm. 6.4), the finite-place identity GZ.7 plans.

items.name: Conjecture 1.1 (Gross–Zagier) and the higher Green functions G_{j+1,f}
items.statement: G_s(z_1, z_2) = −2Σ_{γ∈SL_2(Z)}Q_{s−1}(1 + |z_1 − γz_2|²/(2Im z_1 Im γz_2)) (Legendre function of the second kind), G^m_s = G_s|T_m, and for f = Σc_f(m)q^m ∈ M^!_{−2j}, G_{1+j,f} = Σ_{m>0}c_f(−m)m^jG^m_{j+1}. Conjecture 1.1: if c_f(m) ∈ Z for m < 0 and (z_1, z_2) ∉ Z^j(f) = Σc_f(−m)m^jZ(m) with z_i of discriminant d_i, then (d_1d_2)^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(z_1, z_2) = (w_{d_1}w_{d_2}/4)log|α| for some α ∈ H_{d_1}H_{d_2}.
items.note: Gross–Zagier (1986) V.4 Conj. (4.4); Gross–Kohnen–Zagier (1987) V.1. PAPER-LI-23 proves it at individual CM points using this paper.

items.name: Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.3 and Corollary 1.4: partial averages and exponent-2 class groups
items.statement: Theorem 1.2: let j > 0, d_1 < 0 fundamental, d_2 < 0 with d_1d_2 not a square, C(d_1) = Σ_{Q∈𝒬_{d_1}/Γ}(2/w_Q)z_Q; put (k, H) = (Q(√d_1, √d_2), H_{d_2}(√d_1)) if j is odd and (Q(√d_2), H_{d_2}) if j is even. For every CM point z_2 of discriminant d_2 there are α ∈ H and r ∈ Z_{>0} with (d_1d_2)^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(C(d_1), z_2^σ) = r^{−1}log|α^σ| for all σ ∈ Gal(H/k); r depends only on d_2 (j even) or on d_1, d_2 (j odd) (Remark 1.3). Corollary 1.4: if d_1 < 0 is fundamental with class group trivial or of exponent 2, then (d_1d_2)^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(z_1, z_2) = r^{−1}log|α| with α ∈ H_{d_1}H_{d_2}, for all CM points z_1, z_2 of discriminants d_1, d_2 with (z_1, z_2) ∉ Z^j(f).
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 696; Remark 1.3 and Corollary 1.4, p. 696; Remark 1.5 (Chowla; 52 of 305 fields with |d_1| < 1000), p. 697; Corollary 1.4 as corrected by E5
items.note: Theorem 1.2 is Corollary 7.15 with (d_1, Δ) = (d_1, 1) for even j and (1, d_1) for odd j. Corollary 1.4 is Corollary 7.18.

items.name: Theorems 1.6–1.8: CM value formulas (introduction versions)
items.statement: Theorem 1.6 (j even): G_{j+1,f}(C(d_1), z^+_U) = −2^{j−1}CT⟨Za^j_{d_1}(f), [θ_P, 𝒢^+_N]_{j/2}⟩ for L the trace-zero matrices with Q = det. Theorem 1.7: Φ^j(z^±_U, h, f) = CT⟨f, [θ_P, 𝒢^+_N(τ, h)]_j⟩ for f ∈ M^!_{k−2j,ρ̄_L} and any 𝒢_N with L_1𝒢_N = θ_N(τ, h). Theorem 1.8: Φ^j(Z(U), f)/deg Z(U) = CT⟨f^+, [θ_P, 𝓔^+_N]_j⟩ − L′(ξ_{k−2j}(f), U, 0).
items.note: Special cases of Theorems 7.13, 5.5 and 5.4; worked example G_3(i, (1+i√23)/2) (§8.1).

items.name: Theorem 1.9: a higher-weight Gross–Kohnen–Zagier theorem (introduction version)
items.statement: For D_0 a fundamental discriminant coprime to 2M, Σ_{(4Mm, D_0)=1}⟨Z_κ(m, μ), Z_κ(m_0, μ_0)⟩q^mφ_μ is the Fourier expansion of a cusp form in S_{κ+1/2,ρ_L}(Γ_0(D_0²)).
items.note: Corollary 6.13.

items.name: Lemmas 3.1–3.3: raising/lowering identities, Petersson adjointness and Rankin–Cohen brackets
items.statement: R_k = 2i∂_τ + kv^{−1}, L_k = −2iv²∂_τ̄, −Δ_k = L_{k+2}R_k + k = R_{k−2}L_k, R_{−k}(v^k ḡ) = 0 for holomorphic g. Lemma 3.1: R^j_{k−2}L_k = L_{k+2j}R^j_k + j(k+j−1)R^{j−1}_k. Lemma 3.2: (R_{k−2}h, g)_Pet = 0 for h of moderate growth and g ∈ S_k. The Rankin–Cohen bracket [f, g]_j = Σ_s (−1)^s C(k+j−1, s)C(l+j−1, j−s)f^{(j−s)}g^{(s)} = (−4π)^{−j}Σ_s(−1)^sC(k+j−1, s)C(l+j−1, j−s)(R^{j−s}_k f)(R^s_l g). Lemma 3.3: [f_1, f_2]_j = (4π)^{−j}C(k+l+2j−2, j)f_1R^j_l f_2 + R_{k+l+2j−2}(h) (Viazovska Prop. 3).
items.note: Checked Lemma 3.1 at j = 1.

items.name: Proposition 3.4, Corollary 3.5 and Proposition 3.6: raising Poincaré series and lowering brackets
items.statement: Proposition 3.4: (4πm)^{−1}R_kF_{m,μ}(τ, s, k) = (s + k/2)F_{m,μ}(τ, s, k+2). Corollary 3.5: (4πm)^{−j}R^j_{k−2j}F_{m,μ}(τ, s_0+j, k−2j) = j!F_{m,μ}(τ, s_0+j, k). Proposition 3.6: for f, g harmonic of weights k, l, (−4π)^jL[f, g]_j = C(l+j−1, j)(R^j_kf)(Lg) + (−1)^jC(k+j−1, j)(Lf)(R^j_lg).
items.locator: Proposition 3.6, p. 711; Proposition 3.4 and Corollary 3.5, p. 710
items.note: Checked the cancellation in Proposition 3.6 via C(n, s−1)(n−s+1) = C(n, s)s.

items.name: Lemma 3.7: restriction to finite-index sublattices
items.statement: For M ⊂ L of finite index, res_{L/M}: H_{k,ρ_L} → H_{k,ρ_M}, (f_M)_μ = f_μ̄ if μ ∈ L′/M and 0 otherwise, with ⟨f, θ_L⟩ = ⟨f_{P⊕N}, θ_P ⊗ θ_N⟩ (Bruinier–Yang Lemma 3.1).

items.name: Theorem 3.9 (Theorem 9.4): arithmetic preimages 𝒢_L(τ, h) of binary theta functions
items.statement: For a binary negative definite even lattice L of discriminant D and h ∈ Cl(O_D) there is 𝒢_L(τ, h) ∈ H^!_{1,ρ_L} with L_1𝒢_L = θ_L(τ, h), whose holomorphic coefficients satisfy c^+_L(h, m, μ) = −r^{−1}log|α_L(h, m, μ)| with α_L(h, m, μ) ∈ H_D^× and r depending only on L, for (m, μ) ≠ (0, 0); α_L(h, m, μ) = α_L(1, m, μ)^{[h, k_D]}; and c^+_L(h, 0, 0) = (2/r)log|α_L(h, 0, 0)| + κ(0, 0).
items.locator: Theorem 3.9, p. 714; restated as Theorem 9.4, p. 779; proof pp. 781–783
items.note: Generalizes Ehlen (Duke 2017) Thm. 4.21 and Duke–Li (Duke 2015) to arbitrary binary lattices.

items.name: Lemmas 9.1–9.3: dual bases of weakly holomorphic forms and canonical preimages
items.statement: For N even of even signature and 2k ≡ sig(N) mod 4, with indices (m_i, μ_i), (m̃_i, μ̃_i) dual to bases of M_{k,ρ_N}(Q) and M_{2−k,ρ̄_N}(Q), there are unique bases f_{m,μ} ∈ M^!_{2−k,ρ̄_N}(Q), g_{m,μ} ∈ M^!_{k,ρ_N}(Q) with a_{m,μ}(n, ν) = −b_{n,ν}(m, μ) (Lemma 9.1) and bounded denominators (Lemma 9.2). For N of signature (0, q), k = 2 − q/2, there is a unique 𝒢_N(τ, h) ∈ H^!_{k,ρ_N} with L_k𝒢_N = θ_N(τ, h), normalized at those indices, with Φ_N(h, f_{m,μ}) = c^+_N(h, m, μ) (Lemma 9.3).
items.note: Following Ehlen (2017) §4.3; existence via Bruinier–Funke Cor. 3.8 and Ehlen–Sankaran Prop. 2.12.

items.name: Proposition 9.6, Corollary 9.7 and Borcherds products: see-saw to signature (1, 2)
items.statement: For L = P ⊕ N with P = (Z, x²): there is 𝓕_{m,μ} ∈ M^!_{1/2,ρ̄_L}(Q) with c(0, 0) = 0 and 12Φ_N(h, f_{m,μ}) = Φ_L(z^±_U, h, 𝓕_{m,μ}), with bounded denominators up to any q^{n_0} (Proposition 9.6, via ψ_{0,1} ⊗ f_{m,μ} − x·gψ_{−2,1} ⊗ θ_{N(−1)}). By Borcherds (Thm. 13.3), Φ_L(z, h, 𝓕) = −4log|Ψ_L(z, h, 𝓕)| off the divisor; there is A_0 depending only on N such that Ψ_L(z, h, A_0𝓕_{m,μ}) is defined over Q (Corollary 9.7, via Howard–Madapusi Pera Thm. A).
items.note: Checked the constant-term correction: g ∈ M^!_2 has zero constant term and ⟨ψ_{−2,1}, θ_P⟩ = 0.

items.name: Automorphic Green functions Φ_{m,μ}(z, h, s): Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2, Theorems 4.3–4.4, Proposition 4.5
items.statement: Φ_{m,μ}(z, h, s) = Φ(z, h, F_{m,μ}(τ, s, k)) (regularized theta lift, k = 1 − n/2) equals 2Γ(s + n/4 − 1/2)/Γ(2s)Σ_{λ∈h(μ+L), Q(λ)=m}(m/Q(λ_{z⊥}))^{s+n/4−1/2}F(s + n/4 − 1/2, s − n/4 + 1/2, 2s; m/Q(λ_{z⊥})) for Re s > s_0 = n/4 + 1/2 (Bruinier Thm. 2.14), with meromorphic continuation, a simple pole at s_0, and ΔΦ = ½(s − s_0)(s + s_0 − 1)Φ. Near Z(m, μ) it differs from (2/Γ(s + 1/2 − n/4))Σ Γ̃(0, −4πQ(λ_z)) by a continuous function (Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2); as a current (Δ − ½(s − s_0)(s + s_0 − 1))[Φ_{m,μ}] = −n/(2Γ(s + 1/2 − n/4))δ_{Z(m,μ)} (Theorem 4.3, Oda–Tsuzuki); Φ_{m,μ} ∈ L²(X_K) if V is anisotropic or Re s > 3n/4 > 3/2 (Theorem 4.4), and is characterized by square-integrability and the current equation (Proposition 4.5).
items.locator: Theorem 4.3, p. 717; Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2, Theorem 4.4, Proposition 4.5 and Remark 4.6, pp. 715–718
items.note: The s = s_0 case is also built by the candidate GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22); import it.

items.name: Proposition 4.7 and the higher theta lift Φ^j(z, h, f)
items.statement: For f ∈ H_{k−2j,ρ̄_L}, Φ^j(z, h, f) := (4π)^{−j}Φ(z, h, R^j_{k−2j}f) is a higher Green function for Z^j(f) = Σc^+(−m, μ)m^jZ(m, μ). Proposition 4.7: Φ_{m,μ}(z, h, s_0 + j) = ((4πm)^j j!)^{−1}Φ(z, h, R^j_{k−2j}F_{m,μ}(τ, k−2j)).

items.name: Special divisors Z(m, φ) and small CM cycles Z(U) on orthogonal Shimura varieties
items.statement: For x ∈ V with Q(x) = m > 0, Z(h, x) from H_x(Q)\(D_x × H_x(A_f)/K_{h,x}) → X_K, and Z(m, φ) = Σ_{h∈H_x(A_f)\H(A_f)/K}φ(h^{−1}x)Z(h, x) (Kudla). For U ⊂ V negative definite of dimension 2, T = GSpin(U) ≅ Res(G_m) of an imaginary quadratic field and Z(U) = T(Q)\({z^±_U} × T(A_f)/K_T) with multiplicity 2/w_{K,T}, deg Z(U) = 4/vol(K_T), defined over Q; N = L ∩ U, P = L ∩ U^⊥, θ_L(τ, z^±_U, h) = θ_P(τ) ⊗ θ_N(τ, z^±_U, h).
items.note: PAPER-LI-23 routes the special cycles over totally real fields to the same Part II.

items.name: Lemma 5.1, Corollary 5.2, Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.4: average CM values
items.statement: Lemma 5.1: Φ^j(z^±_U, h, f) = lim_T[(4π)^{−j}∫_{F_T}⟨R^jf, θ_P ⊗ θ_N⟩dμ − A_0 log T], A_0 = (−1)^jCT⟨(f^+)^{(j)}, θ_P ⊗ φ_{0+N}⟩. Lemma 5.3: L(g, U, s) := ([θ_P, E_N(τ, s; 1)]_j, g)_Pet = (4π)^{−j}C(2j−k, j)Γ(s/2+1+j)/Γ(s/2+1)·(θ_P ⊗ E_N(τ, s; 1+2j), g)_Pet, with a Dirichlet series in r(m, μ)b̄(m, μ)m^{−s/2−n/2−j}; it vanishes at s = 0. Theorem 5.4: Φ^j(Z(U), f)/deg Z(U) = CT⟨f^+, [θ_P, 𝓔^+_N]_j⟩ − L′(ξ_{k−2j}(f), U, 0).
items.locator: Theorem 5.4, p. 722; Lemma 5.1, Corollary 5.2 and Lemma 5.3, pp. 720–722
items.note: Checked: R^j_{−k}(θ_P ⊗ E_N(τ, 0; −1)) = 2(−4π)^jL[θ_P, E′_N(τ, 0; 1)]_j via Proposition 3.6, and the unfolding in Lemma 5.3.

items.name: Theorem 5.5 and Corollary 5.6: individual small CM values
items.statement: Theorem 5.5: for f ∈ M^!_{k−2j,ρ̄_L} and h ∈ T(A_f), Φ^j(z^±_U, h, f) = CT⟨f, [θ_P, 𝒢^+_N(τ, h)]_j⟩ for any 𝒢_N ∈ H^!_{1,ρ_N} with L_1𝒢_N = θ_N(τ, h). Corollary 5.6: if f has integral coefficients and Z^j(f) ∩ Z(U) = ∅, then A^jΦ^j(z^±_U, h, f) = −r^{−1}log|α_{U,f}(h)| with α_{U,f}(h) ∈ H_D^×, A the lcm of the levels of P and N and r depending only on L and D; α_{U,f}(h) = α_{U,f}(1)^{[h,k_D]}.
items.note: Uses Madapusi Pera's Lemma 2.6 (GSpin(L̂) is the maximal subgroup preserving L and acting trivially on L′/L) to get K_T ≅ Ô_D^×. Disjointness makes the κ(0, 0)- and A_0-terms vanish.

items.name: Propositions 5.7–5.8, Corollary 5.9 and Theorem 5.10: big CM cycles for real quadratic F
items.statement: For W an F-quadratic space of signature (0, 2) at σ_0 and (2, 0) elsewhere with W_Q ↪ V, Z(W) = Σ_iZ(W_i, σ_i) is defined over Q and Φ^j(Z(W), f) = deg Z(W, σ_0)(−4π)^{−j}∫^reg⟨f, R^j_{−k}(θ_P ⊗ L_1E′_N(τ^Δ, 0; 1))⟩dμ (Proposition 5.7). Proposition 5.8: the Cohen operator 𝒞_j on Hilbert modular forms annihilated by Δ_{k_1}, Δ_{k_2} satisfies (−4π)^jL𝒞_j(g) = C(k_2+j−1, j)(R^j_{k_1,1}L_{k_2,2}g)(τ, τ) + (−1)^jC(k_1+j−1, j)(L_{k_1,1}R^j_{k_2,2}g)(τ, τ). For d = 1 and V = Res_{F/Q}W (signature (2, 2)), Z^j(W) = Z(W_1, σ_1) + (−1)^jZ(W_0, σ_0) and Φ^j(Z^j(W), f)/deg Z(W, σ_0) = CT⟨f^+, 𝒞_j(𝓔^+_L)⟩ − (𝒞_j(E′_L(·, 0; 1)), ξ_{−2j}(f))_Pet (Theorem 5.10), so d_F^{j/2}Φ^j(Z^j(W), f) = C log α with C ∈ Q, α ∈ Q_{>0} for weakly holomorphic f.
items.locator: Theorem 5.10, p. 729; Propositions 5.7–5.8 and Corollary 5.9, pp. 727–729
items.note: Checked Corollary 5.9 from Proposition 5.8 using harmonicity in each variable. Theorem 5.10's proof is omitted as analogous to Theorem 5.4. PAPER-LI-23 uses it for Theorem 1.7.

items.name: Theorem 6.1: CM points in the same imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: For different CM points z_1, z_2 ∈ X(1) of discriminants D_i = t_i²D_0 in Q(√D_0), j > 0 and f ∈ M^!_{−2j} with integral coefficients, there is α ∈ H_D^×, D = lcm(t_1, t_2)²D_0, with |D|^jG_{1+j,f}(z_1^σ, z_2^σ) = −r^{−1}log|α^σ| for all σ ∈ Gal(H_D/Q(√D_0)), r depending only on D. (Via L = M_2(Z) of signature (2, 2), X_K ≅ X(1)², Φ_m(z, s) = −(2/Γ(s))G^m_s(z_1, z_2).)
items.note: Strengthens Viazovska (Theorem 7 of arXiv:1110.4654). As stated it also needs (z_1, z_2) ∉ Z^j(f); see E5.

items.name: Proposition 6.2, Lemma 6.3 and Theorem 6.4: signature (1, 2) and modular curves
items.statement: For L of level 4M in the trace-zero matrices with Q = M det (X_K ≅ Γ_0(M)\H), Φ_{m,μ}(z, s) = −(2/Γ(s + 1/4))G_{M,2s−1/2}(z, Z(m, μ)) via F(a, a+½, c; w) = (1+√w)^{−2a}F(2a, c−½, 2c−1; 2√w/(1+√w)) and Q_{s−1}(t) = Γ(s)²/(2Γ(2s))(2/(1+t))^sF(s, s, 2s; 2/(1+t)) (Proposition 6.2). For D_0 = −4Mm_0 fundamental and g ∈ S_{3/2+2j,ρ_L} with real coefficients, L(g, U, s) = C(s, j)(4πm_0)^{−s/2−1/2−j}L(χ_{D_0}, s+1)^{−1}L(Shim_{m_0,μ_0}(g), s+1+2j) with C(s, j) = 2^{1−s}Γ(s+1+2j)Γ(2j+½)/((4π)^jΓ(2j+1)Γ(s/2+1)) (Lemma 6.3). Theorem 6.4: Φ^j(Z(U), f)/deg Z(U) = CT⟨f^+, [θ_P, 𝓔^+_N]_j⟩ − C(0, j)((4πm_0)^{1/2+j}L(χ_{D_0}, 1))^{−1}L′(Shim_{m_0,μ_0}(ξ_{1/2−2j}f), 1+2j).
items.locator: Theorem 6.4, p. 737; Proposition 6.2, p. 734; Lemma 6.3, pp. 736–737; statement as corrected by E1
items.note: Checked the Gamma-factor simplification in Lemma 6.3 (duplication formula) and the transformation in Proposition 6.2.

items.name: Higher Heegner cycles and their height pairing (Zhang, Xue)
items.statement: For a CM elliptic curve E by √D, Z(E) = Γ − E × {0} + D({0} × E) and S_κ(E) = cΣ_{σ∈P_{2κ−2}}sgn(σ)σ*(Z(E)^{κ−1}) (self-intersection (−1)^{κ−1}); CM-cycles S_κ(x) on 𝒴 for x ∈ 𝒳_0(M) via 𝒳(M′); Green currents g_κ(x) with (πi)^{−1}∂∂̄g_κ = δ_{S_κ(x)}; Ŝ_κ(x) = (S_κ(x̄), g_κ(x)) and ⟨S_κ(x), S_κ(y)⟩ = (−1)^κ(Ŝ_κ(x)·Ŝ_κ(y))_GS = ⟨⟩_fin + ⟨⟩_∞ with ⟨⟩_∞ = ½G_{M,κ}(x, y) (Zhang Prop. 3.4.1); Z_κ(m, μ) = m^{(κ−1)/2}Σ_{x∈Z(m,μ)}S_κ(x).
items.note: Uses Gillet–Soulé arithmetic intersection theory; nothing in the atlas plans higher-dimensional arithmetic Chow groups.

items.name: Theorem 6.5 and Corollary 6.6: global heights of higher Heegner cycles
items.note: Checked the final constant from deg Z(U) = 2√|D_0|L(χ_{D_0}, 1)/π and C(0, j) = 2(4π)^{−j}Γ(2j + ½).

items.name: Proposition 6.7 and Lemma 6.8: Rankin–Cohen coefficients and Legendre polynomials
items.statement: Proposition 6.7: CT⟨f^+_{m_1,μ_1}, [θ_P, 𝓔^+_N]_j⟩ = 2m_1^jΣ_{n≡r_0r_1 (2M), n²≤D_0D_1}κ((D_0D_1 − n²)/(4M|D_0|), 2̃n/√D_0)β_j(n/√(D_0D_1)) with β_j(x) = Σ_s C(j−½, s)C(j, s)x^{2j−2s}(x²−1)^s. Lemma 6.8: β_j = P_{2j}, the Legendre polynomial.
items.locator: Proposition 6.7, p. 741; Lemma 6.8, pp. 742–744; proof as corrected by E2
items.note: Verified β_j = P_{2j} symbolically for j ≤ 5. Mathlib has no Legendre polynomials.

items.name: Theorem 6.12, Corollary 6.13, Lemmas 6.14–6.15 and Proposition 6.16: modularity of height generating series
items.statement: Lemma 6.14: for g ∈ S_{κ+1/2,ρ_L} and R > 0, the part of g supported on (4Mm, R) = 1 lies in S_{κ+1/2,ρ_L}(Γ_0(R²)) (Schwagenscheidt Lemma 2.4). Lemma 6.15: g with b(m, μ) = 0 whenever (4Mm, D_0) = 1 is 0. Proposition 6.16 (refined Borcherds criterion): a formal series h = Σa(m, μ)q^mφ_μ with a(m, μ) = a(m, −μ) and CT⟨f, h⟩ = 0 for every D_0-admissible f ∈ M^!_{3/2−κ,ρ̄_L} agrees on (4Mm, D_0) = 1 with a cusp form in S_{κ+1/2,ρ_L}. Theorem 6.12: there is g ∈ S_{κ+1/2,ρ_L} with b(m, μ) = ⟨Z_κ(m, μ), Z_κ(U)⟩ for (4Mm, D_0) = 1; Corollary 6.13: the restricted generating series lies in S_{κ+1/2,ρ_L}(Γ_0(D_0²)).
items.locator: Theorem 6.12, p. 749; Corollary 6.13, Lemmas 6.14–6.15 and Proposition 6.16, pp. 749–751
items.note: Uses Borcherds's modularity criterion (Duke 1999, Thm. 3.1); checked the symmetrization in the proof of Proposition 6.16.

items.name: Definitions 7.4–7.5 and Remarks 7.6–7.7: twisted divisors, twisted Siegel and Millson theta functions
items.statement: K_Δ = {h ∈ K : (det h, Δ)_{A_f} = 1}, X_{K_Δ} = two copies of SL_2(Z)\H for Δ ≠ 1; Z_Δ(m, h) = Σ_{λ mod Γ_h, Q(λ)=|Δ|m, λ>0}χ_Δ(h^{−1}λ)φ_{rμ}(h^{−1}λ)c(λ, h); for Δ = 1, Z_1(m, h) = P_{D,s} (Remark 7.6). p_z(λ) = −2^{−1/2}(λ, X_1(z)); the Millson theta function θ^𝓜_M(τ, z, h) (weight 1/2); ψ_Δ: S_L → S_{L_Δ}, an intertwiner (Alfes–Ehlen, Bruinier–Ono); θ_{L,Δ} and θ^𝓜_{L,Δ}, K_Δ-invariant, vanishing for Δ < 0, resp. Δ > 0, at level 1 (Remark 7.7); Lemma 7.8: ⟨v, θ_{L,Δ}⟩ = ⟨ψ_Δ(v), θ_{L_Δ}⟩, and likewise for Millson.
items.note: Twists following Bruinier–Ono and Alfes-Neumann–Ehlen.

items.name: Theorem 7.9 and the twisted theta lifts Φ̃^j_Δ
items.locator: Theorem 7.9, p. 758; (7.5), (7.8)–(7.11), pp. 756–760; constant as corrected by E3
items.note: Unfolding, the Laplace transform of M_{1/4,s−1/2} (Erdélyi et al. p. 215 (11)) and (6.9). See E3 for the constant.

items.name: Theorem 7.10: Zagier lifts Za^j_d (Duke–Jenkins, Alfes-Neumann–Schwagenscheidt)
items.statement: For j > 0 and a fundamental discriminant d with (−1)^jd < 0 there is a linear map Za^j_d: H_{−2j} → H_{1/2−j,ρ̃_L} (ρ̃_L = ρ_L for j odd, ρ̄_L for j even) with principal part |d|^{−j/2}Σ_{m>0}c^+_f(−m)Σ_{n|m}(d/n)n^jq^{−|d|m²/(4n²)}φ_{dm²/n²}; Za^j_d(f) is weakly holomorphic iff L(ξ_{−2j}(f), χ_d, j+1) = 0; then, if f^+ has integral principal part, all coefficients of |d|^{j/2}Za^j_d(f) are integers.
items.note: Imports Duke–Jenkins (PAMQ 2008) and Alfes-Neumann–Schwagenscheidt Thm. 1.1 via M_{1/2−j,ρ̃_L} ≅ M^+_{1/2−j}(Γ_0(4)).

items.name: Theorem 7.11: twisted partial averages as theta lifts of Zagier lifts
items.statement: For fundamental discriminants d_1, Δ with (−1)^jd_1 < 0 < (−1)^jΔ, m_1 = |d_1|/4 and f ∈ H_{−2j}: G_{j+1,f}(Z_Δ(m_1, h), (z, h)) = −2^{j−1}Φ̃^j_Δ(z, h, Za^j_{d_1}(f)) for j even and = 2^{j−2}Φ̃^j_Δ(z, h, Za^j_{d_1}(f)) for j odd, using Z_Δ(m_1, h)|T_m = Σ_{n|m}(d_1/n)Z_Δ(m_1m²/n², h) (Gross–Kohnen–Zagier p. 508).
items.locator: Theorem 7.11, p. 761; p. 761; odd-j constant as corrected by E3
items.note: As printed the constant −2^{j−1} is claimed for all j; see E3.

items.name: Lemma 7.12 and Theorem 7.13: twisted partial averages at CM points
items.statement: For d_2 < 0, x_2 = [[r_2/2, 1], [(d_2 − r_2²)/4, −r_2/2]], U = x_2^⊥: N = L ∩ U ≅ (O_{d_2}, −Nm) (Lemma 7.12), P = Z(2/(2 − r_2))x_2, K_T ≅ Ô^×_{d_2}. With N_Δ = ΔL ∩ U, P_Δ = ΔL ∩ U^⊥ (form Q/|Δ|) and 𝒢_{N_Δ}(τ, h) any preimage of θ_{N_Δ}(τ, h): for j even G_{j+1,f}(Z_Δ(m_1, h), (z^+_U, h)) = −2^{j−1}CT⟨ψ_Δ(Za^j_{d_1}(f))_{P_Δ⊕N_Δ}, [θ_{P_Δ}, 𝒢^+_{N_Δ}(τ, h)]_{j/2}⟩, and for j odd = 2^{j−2}CT⟨ψ_Δ(Za^j_{d_1}(f))_{P_Δ⊕N_Δ}, [θ̃_{P_Δ}, 𝒢^+_{N_Δ}(τ, h)]_{(j−1)/2}⟩ with θ̃_{P_Δ} the weight-3/2 theta function with p_{z^+_U}(λ). Remark 7.14: the right-hand side is defined even on the divisors.
items.locator: Theorem 7.13, p. 698; Lemma 7.12, p. 762; Remark 7.14, p. 764; odd case as corrected by E3
items.note: Example 3 (§8.3, j = 1) uses the odd-j constant 1/2 = 2^{j−2}.

items.name: Corollary 7.15 and Lemma 7.16: algebraicity of twisted partial averages
items.statement: Lemma 7.16: K_{T,Δ} = {h ∈ Ô^×_{d_2} : (Nm h, Δ)_{A_f} = 1} has fixed field H_{d_2}(√Δ). Corollary 7.15: if moreover d_1d_2Δ is not a square, f ∈ H_{−2j} has integral principal part and L(ξ_{−2j}(f), χ_{d_1}, j+1) = 0, then |d_1d_2Δ|^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(Z_Δ(m_1, h), (z^+_U, h)) is an integral linear combination of coefficients of 𝒢^+_{N_Δ} and equals −t^{−1}log|α_{U,f,Δ}(h)| with α_{U,f,Δ}(h) ∈ H_{d_2}(√Δ)^×, t depending only on d_2, Δ, and α_{U,f,Δ}(h) = α_{U,f,Δ}(1)^{[h,k_{d_2}]}. For d_1d_2Δ a square it holds when (z^+_U, h) avoids the Hecke translates Z_Δ(m_1, h)|T_m with c_f(−m) ≠ 0.
items.note: The odd-j constant of E3 only changes the rational factor, not algebraicity.

items.name: Lemma 7.17 and Corollary 7.18: individual values for exponent-2 class groups
items.statement: Lemma 7.17: Z(U)_K = (4/w_{d_2})Σ_{Q∈SL_2(Z)\𝒬^0_{d_2}}z_Q. Corollary 7.18: if D′ < 0 is fundamental with class group trivial or of exponent 2, f ∈ M^!_{−2j} has integral principal part, z has discriminant D < 0 and z′ has discriminant D′, and (z, z′) ∉ Z^j(f), then |DD′|^{j/2}G_{j+1,f}(z, z′) = −t^{−1}log|α_f(z)| with α_f(z) ∈ (H_DH_{D′})^× and t depending only on D, D′.
items.locator: Corollary 7.18, p. 767; Lemma 7.17, p. 767; proof pp. 767–768; statement and proof as corrected by E4–E5
items.note: Genus characters separate classes in an exponent-2 group.

routes.reason: GN.2 owns genera, discriminants and local invariants of integral quadratic forms. The local genus characters χ_Δ (Definition 7.1, Lemmas 7.2–7.3) and Gauss's genus theory for exponent-2 class groups are classical binary-form genus theory.

MP.6 plans reusable theta integrals and the local–global comparison. The Siegel–Weil formula for binary lattices (Proposition 3.8) and the Maass-operator identities of the weight-ℓ Eisenstein series belong with it; PAPER-LI-23 routes the signature-(n, 2) formula there.

MP.7 owns half-integral weight forms and their Fourier coefficients and twists. The Shimura lift Shim_{m_0,μ_0}, its Dirichlet series identity and the Skoruppa–Zagier newform isomorphism are half-integral weight theory.

GZ.6 plans 'incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms'. The derivative E′_L(τ, 0; 1) of the weight-1 incoherent Eisenstein series, with coefficients logs of rationals (Kudla–Yang), and its Hilbert analogue (Bruinier–Kudla–Yang) are such kernels.

GZ.7 plans finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local Whittaker functions, with Serre–Tate deformation lengths. The Heegner-divisor stacks, Howard's Cartier-divisor lemma (Lemma 6.10), the pullback decomposition (Lemma 6.11) and the finite intersection formula (Proposition 6.9) are exactly that.
